title: Remains of the Chess Player
next_chapter_hook: Deep within the ruins, an old yet familiar voice suddenly rang out: 'You have finally come... I have been waiting for you, for a very long time.' The master of this voice was exactly the same as the first generation Chess Player recorded in the Tianji Record Fragment.

text.content: At the edge of the Celestial Realm, a void rift gaped like a ferocious wound, spanning between the heavens and chaos. The biting gust carried rotting spiritual energy, cutting painfully at one's face. Chen Ji stood on a floating rubble, his robe corners torn and flapping violently in the wind, yet his gaze remained fixed on the shadowy silhouette flickering within the depths of the rift.

The shadowy outline was ancient and crude, resembling a collapsed ruined palace. The bronze bells hanging from the eaves had long corroded into iron lumps, yet they emitted mournful whispers in the gale. Chen Ji's brow furrowed as the Tianji Record Fragment quivered abruptly in his Mental Sea, igniting unprecedented searing heat— that feeling, like a wandering child returning home, or parched land meeting rain.

dialogue.content: 'Young Master, this place exudes strangeness... Within that ruined hall, fragments of the Great Dao's laws seem to linger.' Mo Xiansheng's voice drifted from the depths of the Mental Sea, carrying a rare gravity. 'Ten thousand years ago, the first Chess Player fell here, at the edge of the Celestial Realm. This is no coincidence.'

text.content: Chen Ji did not respond, spreading his palm open. The yellowed fragment materialized on its own. The cracks along its edges healed at a visible pace, then suddenly stopped—as if some seal had been triggered, only to be forcibly held in place by an even more powerful force.

choice.prompt: The ruined hall lay right before him, the Tianji Record's reaction growing increasingly intense. Should he step in directly, or investigate first?

choices.description: Since the Tianji Record is so eager, it means this opportunity cannot be delayed. How could one retreat from the Chess Player's tomb?
choices.visible_reward: Obtain leads on the Chess Player's legacy first
choices.risk_hint: The ruins may contain mechanisms and prohibitions

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze hardened, and he stepped through the ruined hall's gate. The interior was dark as night, with only the mottled fluorescent moss on the walls emanating a cold, faint glow. The stone tiles beneath his feet creaked and crackled, as if some mechanism had been triggered.

'It comes.' An ancient voice suddenly reverberated through the hall, yet it did not come from any specific direction—it seemed to seep from the void itself. Chen Ji's steps halted abruptly, the Tianji Record Fragment trembling violently.

choices.description: A ten-thousand-year-old ruin must surely hold dangers; rushing in blindly is unwise. First use the Tianji Record to peer three hours into the future, then decide.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain information about the ruins' interior, reducing risk

text.content: Chen Ji drew a deep breath, his fingertip gently touching the fragment. The Tianji Record instantly burst forth dazzling golden light, Chen Ji's vision shifting abruptly—he saw the hall's scene: collapsed stone pillars, scattered Jade Slips, and... a withered skeleton seated upon the altar.

Though ten thousand years had passed since that skeleton perished, it was enveloped in the exact same Great Dao aura as the Tianji Record. In its withered palm it clutched a shattered token, bearing the two characters 'Chess Player'—the identity symbol of the first Chess Player.

The hall was spacious and empty, with only the altar at the very center standing out conspicuously. Cast in bronze, its four corners were carved with images of curled-up prisoners—those prisoners' faces contorted, as if suffering endless torment. The rune patterns inscribed on the platform were identical to the Tianji Record Fragment in Chen Ji's palm—same origin, same root, clearly two sides of the same coin.

Chen Ji approached slowly, his gaze sweeping across the inscription on the altar's edge. Written in ancient seal script, the brushwork was vigorous yet tinged with madness: 'I use Heavenly Fate as fuel, to burn the candle of the Great Dao. Even if Heaven abandons me, I shall not abandon the common people—the first path, break the shackles.'

Break the shackles? Chen Ji's brow arched slightly. The Tianji Record raged and quivered in his Mental Sea, as if trying to break free from its restraints and fling itself into the altar's embrace. Meanwhile, an excruciating tearing pain suddenly shot through his chest—the long-dormant mark deep within his bloodline had been awakened.

dialogue.content: 'This is... Heavenly Fate resonance.' Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly rose sharply, his composure entirely lost, 'Young Master, the blood flowing in your veins is actually the same bloodline as the first Chess Player! He inscribed part of his legacy into the bloodline itself, passing it down through generations, waiting only for the destined one to awaken it!'

text.content: Chen Ji clenched his teeth, letting the power in his blood surge. The burning heat in his chest gradually turned warm, as if a shackle was loosening. He could clearly sense it—the Heavenly Seal on the Tianji Record, the fate pressing down on every Chess Player through the ages.

Just then, the sky outside the hall suddenly darkened. The originally biting strong wind abruptly stilled, and a vast, cold pressure poured down from the heavens above, like an invisible eye piercing through the layers of the Void, gazing at everything within the ruined hall.

dialogue.content: A cold, mechanical voice resonated from within the pressure, devoid of any emotion: "Detecting Tianji Record Fragment entering the ancestral tomb... Chess Player bloodline awakening... Initiating elimination protocol."

text.content: Heavenly Eye! Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. This pressure was all too familiar to him—every time the Tianji Record glimpsed Heavenly Secrets, that prickling sensation of being watched came from this source. He had never imagined this transcendent consciousness would manifest directly at this moment!

choice.prompt: The Heavenly Eye's pressure bears down like collapsing mountains. The inheritance on the altar awaits acceptance. Risk taking the inheritance, or temporarily avoid its edge?

choices.description: Since Heaven has revealed itself, the moment of truth has arrived. Retreat will only tighten the shackles further. Why not use the power of a Chess Player to confront this Heavenly Will head-on!
choices.visible_cost: Face the Heavenly Eye's attack directly
choices.visible_reward: Obtain the first Chess Player's method to break the shackles
choices.risk_hint: The Heavenly Eye's power is immeasurable

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly raised his hand, pressing his palm against the altar. The bronze ancient patterns instantly blazed with blinding golden light, spreading along his meridians throughout his entire body. In that instant, the dormant bloodline within him completely boiled over, merging violently with the Chess Player's inheritance on the altar!

Agonizing pain struck, and Chen Ji felt himself being reshaped by some ancient force. Deep within his Mental Sea, a flood of sealed memories rushed into his mind—the life of the first Chess Player, how he obtained the Tianji Record, how he was chosen by Heaven, and how he was... abandoned by Heaven.

choices.description: Since the Heavenly Eye has appeared, a direct confrontation means certain defeat. Better to retreat one step and preserve what we have—the inheritance can be retrieved eventually.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily abandon this opportunity before you
choices.visible_reward: Preserve yourself and seek another chance

text.content: Chen Ji's body recoiled violently, his toes touching the ground as he prepared to dash out of the hall. However, at that very moment, a golden chain shot out from the Void, precisely wrapping around his ankle. The chain's force was so tremendous it directly dragged him back to the front of the altar!

"There is no escape." The cold voice rang out once more, "Once the Chess Player's bloodline awakens, you have already entered the board. Do you think the shackles can be thrown off simply because you wish it?"

The golden chain radiated scorching heat, burning Chen Ji's ankle flesh until it turned charred black. Yet his face held no panic whatsoever; instead, a cold smile curled at the corner of his mouth—this expression was utterly different from his usual timid, worthless persona.

dialogue.content: "Want me to join the game?" Chen Ji's voice was low and calm, yet carried undeniable sharpness. "Very well, I'll join. It's just that—not everyone who enters the game is necessarily a piece."

text.content: Before his words even finished, the Tianji Record Fragment suddenly burst into brilliant radiance. The cracks along the fragment's edge rapidly healed in the golden light, and a line of ancient text emerged: "The first path has opened; the shackles will break—the cost, Heavenly Fate returns to zero."

Heavenly Fate returns to zero—these four words struck like thunder. Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply; he knew better than anyone what this meant. Heavenly Fate at zero was a certain death sentence! The Heavenly Eye's move was clearly attempting to forcibly end the Chess Player's inheritance by using his life as the price!

The air within the hall solidified to an extreme degree. The golden chains pulled taut beneath Chen Ji's feet, and the Heavenly pressure pressed down on his shoulders like something tangible. Yet the inheritance's light on the altar burned more and more intensely, as if urging him to make a choice. Forward was a deadly trap; retreat was equally a death sentence.

Chen Ji stood motionless on the spot. On that face which usually bore a timid expression, there was now a deathly, serene calm. His eyeballs slowly turned, scanning every detail within the hall—collapsed stone pillars, faded murals, the inscriptions on the altar—all information rapidly integrated within his mind.

"The first path, break the shackles." Chen Ji repeated the inscription in a low voice, then suddenly laughed softly. "So that's how it is... The price of breaking shackles was never Heavenly Fate, but—obsession." His gaze returned to the altar. "The first Chess Player left not a trap, but a key to break the game."

choice.prompt: After discerning the truth, Chen Ji faced the final choice: accept the inheritance at the cost of Heavenly Fate, or take another path by breaking the game with obsession?

choices.description: Heaven wants Heavenly Fate, but I refuse to give it. Pour all my obsession into the Tianji Record, break the shackles with will alone!
choices.visible_reward: Break free from Heavenly Lock, obtain the method to break shackles
choices.risk_hint: Obsession backlash may damage the soul

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, allowing the surging power within him to assault his soul. His obsession was like an invisible blade, fiercely stabbing at that golden chain—the longing for his sister Chen Nian, the hatred for Heaven, the craving for freedom!

The golden chain shattered under the slash of obsession's blade! At the same time, the inheritance light on the altar暴涨, and a profound rune condensed from the void, slowly branding itself on Chen Ji's forehead—that was the will inheritance of the first Chess Player, the true method to break the shackles!

choices.description: Since there's no escape, then let me gamble. What if Heavenly Fate drops to zero? Despair leads to rebirth!
choices.visible_cost: Zero Heavenly Fate triggers instant death
choices.visible_reward: Completely obtain the Chess Player's inheritance
choices.risk_hint: A deadly situation, no one can save

text.content: Chen Ji猛地睁开双眼，双手死死按住祭台。 Heavenly Fate drained like a breached dam, the number plummeting—100, 50, 20, 5... But just as it was about to reach zero, a warm light surged from the depths of the altar, merging explosively with Chen Ji's bloodline!

"Well played." The aged voice rang out again, but no longer that cold mechanical tone—instead carrying a thread of relief. "Ten thousand years of waiting, and finally a madman daring to gamble with Heaven. Accept the inheritance—the first Chess Player's complete legacy—including, the ultimate method to escape Heaven."

The inheritance light illuminated the entire ruined hall, forcibly pushing back the Heavenly Eye's pressure by three points. Chen Ji felt countless profound pieces of information flood his mind—the first Chess Player's lifetime of learning, all his experience opposing Heaven, his final dying bequest: "Trust not Heaven, be no one's piece."

Just as the inheritance was about to complete, a larger rift suddenly tore open in the void outside the hall. A gigantic eye peered through the crack—that eye was dark as an abyss, its pupil swirling with countless scenes of stars being shattered. The Heavenly Eye's本体—had finally descended!

dialogue.content: "Enough." The voice was no longer mechanical broadcast, but carried an unusual hint of fury. "A mere ant dares to steal what was never meant to be yours." That enormous eye slowly turned, its pupil reflecting Chen Ji's figure. "You think you've broken free from the shackles? Laughable... You've merely exchanged them for a more exquisite pair of chains."

text.content: Chen Ji slowly rose to his feet, the dizziness from the inheritance infusion still not fully gone, but his gaze was clearer than ever. He tilted his head to directly face that sky-covering eye, a meaningful smile curling at his lips: "Is that so? Then please enlighten me, Heavenly Eye—when opened?"

The Heavenly Eye fell silent. That dark-as-abyss pupil slightly contracted, as if re-examining this insignificant existence. After a moment, that icy voice sounded again: "Chess Player... Interesting. I hope your chess game can last until the day you witness the truth."

Before the words even faded, that enormous eye and its sky-covering pressure vanished together. The ruined hall returned to silence, only that inscription on the altar still glowing faintly: "Even if Heaven abandons me, I shall not abandon the living—the first path, opened." Chen Ji lowered his gaze to his palm, where the Tianji Record Fragment radiated a soft light, its cracks healing another fraction.

He deeply exhaled a breath of turbid air, turning to leave the ruins. However, just then, an aged yet familiar voice suddenly echoed from the depths of the altar—the voice's owner was exactly identical to the first generation Chess Player recorded in the Tianji Record Fragment: "You've finally come... I've been waiting, for a very long time."

Chen Ji's footsteps halted abruptly, whipping around. The inscription on the altar was slowly fading away, replaced by a illusory figure. That figure's face was blurred, surrounded by a aura of the Great Dao sourced from the same origin as the Tianji Record, quietly hovering above the altar, as if it had waited ten thousand years for this moment.

"Do not be surprised." That figure's voice was aged and weary. "This is merely a wisp of remnant will I left within the inheritance. The true me perished beneath Heaven's Judgment ten thousand years ago. But before that, I sealed all the truths within this path—including, Heaven's Eye's true purpose."

Chen Ji listened quietly, his expression unchanged, yet storms raged within his heart. The first chess player from ten thousand years ago—that existence which had played against the Heavenly Dao—had left clues in such a manner. He understood that the moment he stepped into this ruins, he had already entered a chess game spanning ten thousand years.

Outside the ruined hall, violent winds rose once more. Chen Ji cast one final glance at the suspended spectral image, carving every piece of information into the depths of his Mental Sea. The legacy of the first chess player, the preliminary glimpse of methods to break chains, the threat of the Eye of Heavenly Dao—all of this served as a reminder: the chess game has been set, and a move once made cannot be undone. And he, Chen Ji, would be the sole chess player upon this eternal board who plays not by conventional rules.
